article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Mendo Purps IBL
Breeder: BC Bud Depot
THC Content: Moderate to high
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Grape, berries, caramel, earthy pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 7–8 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Dense, productive harvests
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Easy to moderate

Few purple cannabis strains carry the historical weight of The Purps . Long before violet flower became a routine feature of dispensary menus, Mendocino County growers were circulating a coveted purple clone prized for grape-like flavor, unusual coloration, and an uplifting high that differed sharply from the heavy sedation often associated with purple weed. BC Bud Depot eventually obtained this Mendocino Purps material and spent approximately two years developing it into a reproducible seed line, releasing the result as The Purps. The breeder still lists it today as a Mendo Purps IBL and describes dense purple flowers, a deep grape taste, and a soaring effect with little burnout.

Its reputation extends beyond appearance. The cultivar earned third place in the Sativa category at the High Times Cannabis Cup in both 2007 and 2009, while BC Bud Depot lists it among its award-winning strains and notes its 2007 Strain of the Year recognition. Those accolades helped establish The Purps as one of the defining purple marijuana varieties of the 2000s. Where many contemporary purple hybrids rely on Cookies , Gelato , or modern dessert genetics, this cultivar reflects an older Northern California tradition built around Mendocino cannabis, natural pigmentation, fruit-forward aroma, and an unusually clear mental effect.
Genetics and Lineage

The most accurate breeder designation for The Purps is Mendo Purps IBL. BC Bud Depot’s current regular-seed listing identifies it exactly that way rather than describing it as a conventional cross between two named parents. The starting material was the celebrated Mendocino Purps clone, a Northern California cultivar that circulated for years as clone-only cannabis before a seed version became widely available. Weedmaps likewise distinguishes the original clone from BC Bud Depot’s later seed work, noting that the company stabilized the genetics into what became The Purps.

An IBL, or inbred line, is developed through repeated selection and breeding within the same genetic family rather than by simply crossing two unrelated strains. In this case, the objective was to preserve recognizable Mendocino Purps qualities—purple coloration, grape flavor, strong resin production , and its characteristic high—while allowing growers to reproduce the plant from seed. Older secondary descriptions occasionally give more complicated parentage, but BC Bud Depot’s own current catalog is the stronger source and simply identifies the strain as Mendo Purps IBL.

The precise origin of the original Mendocino clone remains less certain. It arose from Northern California’s Emerald Triangle cannabis culture, and its original breeder has never been reliably established in public documentation. That uncertainty should not be filled with invented ancestry. The history that can be stated confidently is that Mendo Purps existed as a sought-after clone, BC Bud Depot obtained it, and the company subsequently produced the seed line recognized internationally as The Purps.
Effects and Experience

The Purps contradicts the expectation that deeply colored weed must be overwhelmingly sedating. Its opening phase tends to be bright and mentally elevated, often bringing a noticeable increase in mood, sociability, and sensory enjoyment. BC Bud Depot describes the effect as uplifting and soaring with essentially no burnout, language that also helps explain why the strain competed successfully in sativa categories despite its mixed genetic character. Music, conversation, creative hobbies, relaxed outdoor activity, or an unstructured afternoon can fit comfortably with this kind of cannabis experience.

Physical relaxation gradually becomes more apparent after the cerebral peak develops. Muscles may loosen and activity can feel less urgent, but moderate consumption does not necessarily result in the abrupt couch-lock associated with heavier indica varieties. The balance can therefore feel surprisingly functional for such dark-purple marijuana. Larger doses change that equation, and some consumers find the later phase considerably heavier, particularly when using potent flower or consuming repeatedly over a short period.

The original breeder does not assign a universal THC percentage to the current seed line. That is preferable to treating one laboratory result as representative of an entire strain. Cannabinoid concentration varies with phenotype, cultivation method, harvest maturity, curing, and storage. The Purps earned its reputation through the quality and character of its high rather than through an advertised laboratory number.
Medical Benefits

No controlled clinical study has evaluated The Purps as a specific medical cannabis cultivar. Any discussion of possible therapeutic value therefore has to remain grounded in its general THC-dominant effect pattern rather than claiming that the strain treats a particular condition. Its combination of mood elevation and later physical relaxation may appeal to some consumers looking for marijuana that eases mental tension without beginning with strong sedation.

People who prefer evening or late-afternoon cannabis may also appreciate how the experience develops. Initial mental uplift can transition into a calmer body state, and appetite may become stronger as the session progresses. These characteristics are among the reasons similar THC-rich hybrids are sometimes chosen by consumers dealing with temporary stress, reduced appetite, or everyday physical tension.

Responses can differ dramatically, however. Larger quantities may cause dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, impaired coordination, or excessive sleepiness, particularly among people with limited THC tolerance. Medical cannabis decisions should therefore be based on the chemical analysis of the actual flower and qualified healthcare advice rather than the reputation of a strain name.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Deep grape is the signature flavor associated with The Purps, and BC Bud Depot continues to make that characteristic central to its description of the cultivar. The fruit quality is darker than the bright candy grape found in many recent hybrids. Ripe berries, grape skins, floral sweetness, damp earth, and fresh pine can emerge around the core aroma, giving the flower a distinctly natural and somewhat old-school character.

More subtle flavors become noticeable during consumption. Historical descriptions of Mendocino Purps-derived flower include buttery caramel, coffee, wood, and floral pine, creating considerably more complexity than the strain’s reputation as simply “purple grape weed” implies. The sweeter fruit tends to dominate the first impression, while earthy, woody, and lightly roasted notes become easier to detect on the finish.

There is no definitive breeder-issued terpene panel for the original BC Bud Depot line. Myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, pinene, and limonene are plausible contributors to individual examples, but terpene dominance should never be inferred solely from flavor. Soil composition, light intensity, environmental stress, phenotype, harvest timing, and curing technique can all alter the final aromatic chemistry.
Growing Information

The Purps was bred for both indoor and outdoor cultivation. BC Bud Depot currently lists the regular seed version at approximately seven to eight weeks indoors with outdoor maturity around late September. Older breeder material preserved by strain archives placed outdoor maturity somewhat later, around mid-October, while the company’s newer feminized listing gives an indoor window of roughly eight to nine weeks. Growers should therefore treat those ranges as phenotype- and version-dependent rather than expecting every plant to finish on exactly the same date.

Plants can develop substantial side branching and respond well to canopy management. Some phenotypes stretch noticeably once flowering begins, while others remain stockier and more indica-like. That variability makes early observation important. Topping and low-stress training can create a broader canopy, while a screen helps support productive lateral branches and keeps vigorous plants from developing an uneven indoor structure.

Color intensifies as flowers mature. Green growth may transition toward burgundy, violet, and deep purple as anthocyanin pigmentation becomes more visible. Genetics determine whether a plant has the capacity to turn purple; cool nighttime temperatures can enhance the expression in some individuals but should not be used aggressively enough to compromise plant health. Dense mature flowers also benefit from strong airflow, particularly where cool autumn conditions bring rising humidity.

BC Bud Depot does not currently publish a standardized yield in grams per square meter or grams per outdoor plant, describing the harvest instead as dense and productive. That makes more sense than promising a universal figure. Root volume, vegetative period, training, lighting, climate, and phenotype can produce enormous differences in final harvest size.
FAQ
What are the genetics of The Purps?
BC Bud Depot identifies The Purps as a Mendo Purps IBL. It was developed from the legendary Mendocino Purps clone rather than from a recently created two-parent hybrid.
Is The Purps the same as Mendocino Purps?

They are closely connected but historically distinct. Mendocino Purps was the original Northern California clone-only cannabis variety. BC Bud Depot worked with that material and stabilized it into seed form as The Purps.
Is The Purps indica or sativa?

BC Bud Depot classifies it broadly as a sativa/indica hybrid rather than assigning a precise percentage. Its flowers and growth can display substantial indica characteristics, while the clear, uplifting high contributed to its placement in sativa competitions.
What does The Purps taste like?

Grape is the defining flavor, complemented by berries, earthy pine, floral sweetness, wood, and occasionally caramel or coffee-like notes. The breeder specifically emphasizes its lingering deep-purple grape character.
How long does The Purps take to flower?

The current regular-seed version is listed at approximately seven to eight weeks indoors, while BC Bud Depot’s feminized version is listed around eight to nine weeks. Outdoor harvest generally falls between late September and mid-October depending on phenotype and growing conditions.
Final Thoughts on The Purps

The Purps helped define what growers and consumers came to expect from premium purple marijuana. Its appeal was never limited to anthocyanin coloration. Mendocino genetics gave the cultivar a deep grape-and-berry identity, while the high remained clearer and more uplifting than the heavy sedative stereotype attached to many purple strains. BC Bud Depot’s work turning the once clone-only Mendo Purps into a stable seed line allowed those traits to reach growers far beyond Northern California.

Its awards reinforce that historical significance. The Purps earned recognition as a leading strain in 2007 and placed in the High Times Cannabis Cup’s sativa division in both 2007 and 2009. Modern cannabis offers countless purple hybrids with higher advertised THC figures and more elaborate family trees, but few carry the same connection to Mendocino’s early purple-cannabis culture. For enthusiasts interested in classic North American weed genetics, The Purps remains an important bridge between a legendary regional clone and the internationally available purple strains that followed.
